_note: Iteration 5: human cost data. Incidents and site totals from the incident research; coordinates and footprint series from the geography research; exposure estimator inputs from the exposure research. Built by tools/iter5_human.py.
lead: These are the people behind the metals: miners buried in landslides in Kachin and Rubaya, smelter workers burned in Morowali, children working in Cerro Rico. Each death below is dated and sourced, and counted once.
caveat: Every number is a minimum: most deaths at informal mines are never recorded, and some tolls are disputed. These are places in the supply chains this site traces. For most of them the link into fusion is likely or a hypothesis, not proven; each site's case file says which.

incidents.place: Pangwa, Chipwi Township, Kachin State, Myanmar (mining plot No. 3, near Chinese border post No. 3)
incidents.summary: A landslide at a rare earth mine in Pangwa buried workers; early reports gave 5-7 dead, and RFA later reported more than 20 killed, including three Chinese citizens.
incidents.cause: Landslide at in-situ leaching rare earth mine in rainy season; acid pumped into hillsides weakens soil (Global Witness); militia-controlled Special Region 1
incidents.quote: A June 4 landslide killed more than 20 people, including three Chinese citizens.

incidents.place: Pang War (Pangwa), Chipwi Township, Kachin State, Myanmar
incidents.affected_desc: 30 workers trapped
incidents.summary: A second landslide at around midnight overran a living area and processing facility; 15 bodies were recovered and 14 workers were still missing.
incidents.cause: Landslide after continuous rainfall at unregulated rare earth mine
incidents.quote: "Fifteen bodies have been found so far. Two women were among them" ... A Chinese national and 13 other workers were still missing

incidents.place: Pangwa area, Chipwi Township, Kachin State, Myanmar
incidents.affected_desc: over a dozen injuries and around 50 deaths across the May-July 2024 rainy season (includes the 4 and 19 June landslides)
incidents.summary: Myanmar Witness attributed around 50 deaths and over a dozen injuries to landslides around the Pangwa mines in the 2024 rainy season. This is an aggregate that contains inc-001 and inc-002; do not add them together.
incidents.cause: Landslides linked to mine expansion, deforestation and soil degradation
incidents.quote: increased landslides and altered mountain landscapes from May to July 2024 (rainy season), which reportedly caused over a dozen injuries and around 50 deaths
incidents.notCounted: Estimate for the whole 2024 rainy season; overlaps the dated Pangwa landslides, so not added.

incidents.place: Kachin Special Region 1 (Pangwa/Chipwi), Kachin State, Myanmar
incidents.affected_desc: two miners, one a 15-year-old boy, died soon after being discharged from work with severe gastrointestinal illness; families blame chemical exposure (not diagnosed)
incidents.summary: Global Witness obtained interviews with the families of two miners, one aged 15, who died soon after leaving work. Their families believe chemical exposure caused the deaths, but no diagnosis was made.
incidents.cause: Suspected exposure to leaching chemicals (ammonium sulphate, oxalic acid); undiagnosed
incidents.quote: One was a newlywed husband and father. The other was a 15-year-old boy.

incidents.place: Kachin Special Region 1 (Pangwa/Chipwi), Kachin State, Myanmar
incidents.affected_desc: teenage boys leaving school for the mines; young women recruited via social media for sexual and domestic services to Chinese workers (no count)
incidents.summary: Global Witness reported teenage boys leaving school to work in the mines, and young women recruited online to provide sexual and domestic services to Chinese mine staff. It gave no numbers.
incidents.cause: Mining boom economy under militia control
incidents.quote: teenage boys are leaving school to try their luck in the mines, while young women are recruited via ads on social media to provide sexual and domestic services

incidents.place: Seinlon village, Momauk Township, Kachin State, Myanmar
incidents.affected_desc: three anti-mining protesters held for three days
incidents.summary: KIA Brigade 3 detained three people who were protesting against rare earth mining, accused them of being military informants, and held them for three days.
incidents.cause: Kachin Independence Army (KIA) Brigade 3
incidents.quote: In April 2023, KIA Brigade 3 detained three active protesters against rare earth mining, accusing them of being military informants, and held them for three days

incidents.place: Hpare village, Chipwi Township, Kachin State, Myanmar
incidents.affected_desc: civilians from Hpare village (number not given)
incidents.summary: The KIO/KIA detained civilians from Hpare village, a settlement of war-displaced Kachin people, after they opposed rare earth mining there.
incidents.cause: Kachin Independence Organization/Army
incidents.quote: In October 2023, KIO/KIA also detained civilians from Hpare village.

incidents.place: Chipwi area, Kachin State, Myanmar
incidents.affected_desc: nearly 300 local residents with skin disease attributed to rare earth mining waste (RFA Burmese, 23 Nov 2023, cited by ISP-Myanmar)
incidents.summary: RFA Burmese reported that nearly 300 local residents had skin diseases that they attribute to rare earth mining waste.
incidents.cause: Rare earth mining waste and leaching chemicals
incidents.quote: [Nearly 300 Locals in Kachin Suffer from Skin Diseases Due to Rare Earth Mining Wastes] (ISP-Myanmar English translation of RFA Burmese headline)

incidents.place: Pangwa town, Chipwi Township, Kachin State, Myanmar (KIA-controlled)
incidents.affected_desc: a Chinese owner, four workers and two residents killed; five of the injured critical
incidents.summary: Explosives stored for rare earth mining blew up at a Chinese-owned depot in Pangwa, killing at least seven people and injuring 11.
incidents.cause: Explosion at Chinese-owned mining explosives storage facility
incidents.quote: At least seven people, including a Chinese owner, four workers and two residents, were killed and 11 were injured during an explosion at an explosives storage facility in Kachin State's Pangwa town

incidents.place: Kachin State rare earth mining area, Myanmar
incidents.summary: A worker interviewed by Yale e360 said a worker was buried during excavation in 2025, and his body was found only after rain and landslides washed the soil away.
incidents.cause: Excavation accident
incidents.quote: This year, there was an accident during excavation and a worker was buried

incidents.place: Mong Khark area, Mong Bawk (Mong Pawk) Township, Eastern Shan State, Myanmar (UWSA-controlled)
incidents.affected_desc: more than 40 acres of farmland destroyed by flood sludge (further floods 5 and 10 Aug 2025)
incidents.summary: Floods carried sludge from rare earth mines over farmland downstream. More than 40 acres of rice, corn, peanut and soybean fields were destroyed, and replanted crops were lost again in August.
incidents.cause: Runoff from UWSA-area rare earth mines during heavy rain
incidents.quote: more than 40 acres of farmland have been destroyed downstream of rare earth mines in the Mong Khark area of Mong Bawk Township

incidents.place: Kok and Sai rivers, northern Thailand (downstream of Shan State mines)
incidents.affected_desc: an estimated 1.3 billion baht ($40 million) in losses to farming, fishing and tourism
incidents.summary: Toxic runoff from rare earth mines in Shan State polluted rivers flowing into northern Thailand, causing an estimated $40 million in losses to local farming, fishing and tourism.
incidents.cause: Unregulated rare earth mining upstream in Shan State
incidents.quote: causing an estimated 1.3 billion baht ($40 million) in losses across the farming, fishing and tourism industries

incidents.place: Bibatama, Rubaya mining area, Masisi territory, North Kivu, DRC
incidents.affected_desc: local news site Mines.cd reported over 300 fatalities
incidents.summary: A major slope failure at the unlicensed Rubaya coltan diggings killed at least 21 people. A local outlet reported more than 300 deaths.
incidents.cause: Landslide at artisanal coltan pits under M23 control
incidents.quote: killed at least 21 people, but in all probability many more people died. Local news site Mines.cd reports over 300 fatalities.

incidents.place: Luwowo site, Gasasa, Rubaya mining area, Masisi territory, North Kivu, DRC
incidents.affected_desc: M23-appointed governor's spokesperson later put the toll at 226; victims included miners, women and children
incidents.summary: Two successive landslides on 28-29 January collapsed hand-dug tunnels at Rubaya. At least 200 people died; a later rebel-administration count gave 226.
incidents.cause: Tunnel collapse after heavy rain at unregulated M23-controlled mine
incidents.quote: a network of hand-dug tunnels collapsed, killing at least 200 artisanal miners and trapping an unknown number who remain missing

incidents.place: Kasasa site, Rubaya mining area, Masisi territory, North Kivu, DRC
incidents.affected_desc: about 70 children among the dead (DRC Ministry of Mines); M23 official claimed only about five died
incidents.summary: Another landslide at Rubaya killed more than 200 people, about 70 of them children, according to the DRC mines ministry. M23 disputed the figure.
incidents.cause: Landslide after heavy rain at M23-controlled artisanal mine
incidents.quote: more than 200 people, including children, had died in the disaster, which occurred on March 3 at around 3 p.m.

incidents.place: Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu, gold), DRC
incidents.affected_desc: 18 artisanal miners summarily killed at Rubaya and Lomera combined (10 beaten to death, 2 shot, 6 abducted and found dead)
incidents.summary: Amnesty documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 fighters and allied guards at Rubaya and the Lomera gold site. The report does not give a split between the two sites.
incidents.cause: M23 fighters and allied security guards
incidents.quote: The organization documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners at the Rubaya and Lomera mines.
incidents.notCounted: Combines Rubaya with the Lomera gold site, so not added to Rubaya's total.

incidents.place: Coltan mines near Rubaya, North Kivu, DRC
incidents.affected_desc: miners forced to dig, often underground for more than a week at a time; seven miners described detention and ransom under threat of forced recruitment (26 interviewees)
incidents.summary: Amnesty found that M23 forced miners to dig coltan, often keeping them underground for more than a week. It also used the mines to detain miners for ransom under threat of sending them to military training.
incidents.quote: M23 fighters forced miners to dig minerals, often making them work underground for more than a week at a time in coltan mines near Rubaya

incidents.place: PT Indonesia Tsingshan Stainless Steel (ITSS) smelter, IMIP, Morowali, Central Sulawesi
incidents.summary: A furnace explosion and fire during repair work at a Tsingshan-controlled smelter at IMIP killed 21 workers and injured at least 38.
incidents.cause: Oxygen tank explosion during furnace repair; PT ITSS (Tsingshan)
incidents.quote: A fire at a Chinese-owned nickel smelter in Sulawesi on 24 December 2023 killed 21 people.

incidents.place: PT Gunbuster Nickel Industry (GNI) smelter, North Morowali, Central Sulawesi
incidents.summary: An explosion and fire at the GNI smelter in late December 2022 killed two employees.
incidents.cause: Smelter explosion/fire; PT GNI (Jiangsu Delong)
incidents.quote: In late December, an explosion at the GNI as the mineral processing and refining plant in Morowali killed two employees.

incidents.place: PT Gunbuster Nickel Industry (GNI) smelter, North Morowali, Central Sulawesi
incidents.affected_desc: one Indonesian and one Chinese worker killed
incidents.summary: Clashes between Indonesian and Chinese workers broke out after a labour protest over safety at the GNI smelter, and two workers were killed.
incidents.cause: Clash after labour protest over safety and contracts at PT GNI
incidents.quote: An Indonesian and a Chinese worker died after a clash broke out following a protest staged by a labour group

incidents.place: PT Dexin Steel Indonesia, IMIP, Morowali, Central Sulawesi
incidents.affected_desc: Public Citizen GTW describes the same late-2024 IMIP blast: crane operator Gunawan died and another worker was injured; a BHRRC headline reports two Dexin workers died after the explosion and later repair work
incidents.summary: An explosion and fire at the Dexin Steel plant in IMIP killed one worker and badly injured another.
incidents.cause: Explosion at waste pool / fire; PT Dexin Steel Indonesia
incidents.quote: PT Dexin Steel Indonesia, experienced an explosion leading to a fire on Friday (25/10/2024. The incident resulted in one fatality and one severe injury.

incidents.place: Tailings storage facility, IMIP, Morowali, Central Sulawesi
incidents.affected_desc: four excavator operators buried: one survived, two dead, one missing
incidents.summary: A landslide of nickel tailings at IMIP buried four contractor workers; two were found dead and one is missing, feared dead.
incidents.cause: Tailings facility collapse after heavy rain (activists allege dam failure); contractor PT MIKI for PT QMB New Energy Materials and PT Huayue Nickel Cobalt
incidents.quote: The landslide buried four excavator operators under toxic mine waste. One worker survived, while two were found dead. The fourth worker remains missing

incidents.place: PT Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park (IWIP) mine site, Central Halmahera, North Maluku
incidents.summary: A dump truck with failed brakes crashed into two other trucks at the IWIP nickel mine, injuring 11 workers. The union said a worker had died at IWIP the previous year.
incidents.cause: Brake failure; production-target pressure alleged by union
incidents.quote: Eleven mine workers were injured in a truck crash at the nickel mine site of PT Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park (IWIP)

incidents.place: Central Sulawesi province (incl. Morowali district), Indonesia
incidents.affected_desc: 305,191 respiratory infection diagnoses in Central Sulawesi in 2024 (262,160 in 2023); 57,190 in Morowali district in 2024
incidents.summary: Komnas HAM cited provincial health data showing 305,191 respiratory infection diagnoses in Central Sulawesi in 2024, up 26% on 2023. These are all respiratory infections in the province, not cases proven to be caused by nickel.
incidents.cause: Dust and emissions from nickel mining and smelting (association, not attribution)
incidents.quote: respiratory infections reached 305,191 diagnoses in 2024, a 26% increase over the 262,160 cases recorded in 2023

incidents.place: IWIP, Weda Bay, Central Halmahera, North Maluku
incidents.affected_desc: 19 of 23 workers interviewed had heard of a coworker dying suddenly; 2 witnessed it (typical age 26-35)
incidents.summary: Researchers from Sembada Bersama interviewed 23 IWIP workers. Nineteen had heard of a coworker dying suddenly, which the researchers link to 12-hour shifts of about 60 hours a week.
incidents.cause: Excessive working hours (about 60 h/week)
incidents.quote: Among 23 workers interviewed, 19 said they had heard of a coworker dying suddenly, while two said they had witnessed such incidents firsthand

incidents.place: Maba Sangaji village, East Halmahera, North Maluku
incidents.affected_desc: 27 Indigenous villagers arrested, 16 released next day, 11 detained, charged and jailed on 16 Oct 2025; one beaten during interrogation (Amnesty)
incidents.summary: Police arrested 27 Maba Sangaji villagers who held a ritual protest against nickel mining on their customary land. Eleven were charged, then convicted and jailed in October 2025.
incidents.cause: North Maluku police; mining company PT Position (Harum Energy subsidiary), not an IWIP tenant
incidents.quote: police arrested 27 villagers from Maba Sangaji on May 18, accusing them of making threats, but released 16 the next day while detaining 11 others

incidents.place: Halmahera, North Maluku (Weda Bay Nickel concession, Eramet/Tsingshan)
incidents.affected_desc: about 500 uncontacted Hongana Manyawa people whose forest territory overlaps the Weda Bay Nickel concession
incidents.summary: Survival International said Weda Bay Nickel's mining is destroying the forest of about 500 uncontacted Hongana Manyawa people. Footage shows some coming out of the forest to beg miners for food.
incidents.cause: Weda Bay Nickel (Eramet / Tsingshan) mine expansion
incidents.quote: Eramet ... has known of the severe risks to the 500 uncontacted Indigenous people for more than 10 years

incidents.place: Man Maw tin mining area, Wa State (UWSA), Shan State, Myanmar
incidents.summary: An explosion at a Man Maw mining site killed nine workers and injured 30, and the Wa authorities ordered a safety review.
incidents.cause: Mine explosion (cause not published)
incidents.quote: On 4 May, an explosion at a mining site in Man Maw tragically killed nine workers, injuring a further 30.

incidents.place: Grasberg Block Cave, Mimika, Central Papua, Indonesia
incidents.affected_desc: about 800,000 t of wet material entered the mine; 2 bodies found 20 Sep, 5 found 5 Oct 2025
incidents.summary: A mud rush of about 800,000 tonnes flooded the Grasberg Block Cave and killed seven workers.
incidents.cause: Mud rush from former open pit into block cave; PT Freeport Indonesia
incidents.quote: We are grieving for our seven coworkers lost in this tragic incident

incidents.place: Big Gossan underground training facility, Grasberg district, Papua, Indonesia
incidents.summary: The roof of a non-operational tunnel collapsed during a safety training session, killing 28 miners and injuring ten. A union mission blamed management negligence.
incidents.cause: Tunnel roof collapse; PT Freeport Indonesia
incidents.quote: killing 28 miners and injuring ten others

incidents.place: Timika, Papua, Indonesia
incidents.affected_desc: Amnesty names two protesting Freeport workers killed (Petrus Ayamiseba, Leo Wandagau); NPR reports one killed and six wounded
incidents.summary: Police fired on striking Freeport workers trying to stop replacement workers. Amnesty records two protesting workers killed.
incidents.cause: Indonesian police
incidents.quote: the killing of Petrus Ayamiseba and Leo Wandagau, two protesting workers employed at the gold and copper mining company Freeport in Timika on October 10, 2011

incidents.place: PT Freeport Indonesia office, Kuala Kencana, Timika, Papua
incidents.affected_desc: New Zealand employee Graeme Wall killed
incidents.summary: Gunmen attacked a Freeport office, killing one staff member and wounding six other people.
incidents.cause: Armed group (suspected Papuan separatists)
incidents.quote: One staff member of PT Freeport Indonesia was killed and six other people were wounded when attackers opened fire

incidents.place: Grasberg open pit, Mimika, Central Papua
incidents.affected_desc: worker Simson Mulia, 48
incidents.summary: An unknown assailant shot dead a Freeport worker inside the Grasberg open-pit mining area.
incidents.cause: Unknown assailant
incidents.quote: A worker at PT Freeport Indonesia was fatally shot by an unknown assailant in the open-pit mining area of Grasberg Mining

incidents.place: Nui Phao mine, Dai Tu district, Thai Nguyen, Vietnam
incidents.affected_desc: households in high-risk zones still not relocated after 13 years; company plans to resettle 1,925 households over the mine's life
incidents.summary: A ministry inspection fined Nui Phao Mining for violations, including failing to move households out of areas at high risk of environmental impact.
incidents.cause: Nui Phao Mining Co (Masan)
incidents.quote: had still not completed ground clearance and the move of households in areas of high risk of environmental impact

incidents.place: Agricultural soils near tungsten mines, southern Jiangxi, China
incidents.affected_desc: arsenic and cadmium hazard quotients above 1 at study sites; hazard index above 10 at site FJ-S
incidents.summary: A soil study near southern Jiangxi tungsten mines found arsenic and cadmium levels that pose non-cancer and cancer health risks, with chronic-poisoning-level risk at one site.
incidents.cause: Heavy metals from tungsten mining
incidents.quote: The HI value exceeded 10 at site FJ-S, indicating health risks and risk of chronic poisoning.

incidents.place: Ganzhou, Jiangxi, China
incidents.affected_desc: more than 100 landslides reported in Ganzhou rare earth areas (no casualty count given)
incidents.summary: Global Witness reported more than 100 landslides in China's Ganzhou rare earth region. It gave no casualty count.
incidents.cause: Ion-adsorption rare earth leaching
incidents.quote: in China's Ganzhou more than 100 landslides have been reported

incidents.place: Lintang, Longnan, Ganzhou, Jiangxi, China
incidents.affected_desc: acid leachate from a burst pond entered soil and downstream water
incidents.summary: A pond at an illegally run rare earth operation burst, sending acid into the surrounding soil and water downstream.
incidents.cause: Rare earth operator illegally using abandoned leaching ponds
incidents.quote: a rare earth mining operation located in Lintang, Ganzhou, had been illegally using and managing abandoned ponds. A pond burst, which resulted in acid leaching into surrounding soil and water

incidents.place: Puinawai reserve / Guainía, Colombia
incidents.affected_desc: whole Puinawai families coerced to work illegal coltan/tungsten mines (no count)
incidents.summary: ICIJ reported that traffickers coerced whole families of the Indigenous Puinawai people to work illegal mines controlled by FARC guerrillas and paramilitaries.
incidents.cause: FARC, paramilitaries and drug-trafficking gangs
incidents.quote: traffickers have coerced whole families from the Puinawai tribe to work the mines

incidents.place: Mecklenburg mine (Chromex Mining / Afarak), near Burgersfort, Limpopo, South Africa
incidents.affected_desc: 600 community members protested; 2 shot with rubber bullets; 3 people arrested (charges later handled by community-funded lawyer)
incidents.summary: Security guards fired rubber bullets at the backs of protesters as they walked away from a peaceful protest at a chrome mine. Two people were injured, and the protest leader and the two injured were then arrested.
incidents.cause: Mine security personnel; South African police (arrests)
incidents.quote: the security personnel fired rubber bullets from close range at the backs of people leaving, injuring, according to activists interviewed for this report, two people

incidents.place: Makgomo Chrome plant, near Burgersfort, Sekhukhune, Limpopo, South Africa
incidents.affected_desc: six villagers arrested; police used water cannon and rubber bullets on the protest camp
incidents.summary: Police dispersed residents who had camped outside a chrome plant since February to demand a stake in the mine, and six villagers were arrested.
incidents.cause: South African Police Service, with private security
incidents.quote: the arrest of six villagers when tensions erupted in chaos on 3 May

incidents.place: Cerro Rico, Potosí, Bolivia
incidents.affected_desc: 96 mining deaths in Potosí department in 2025 to 3 Oct, at least 90 of them inside Cerro Rico (unpublished police data)
incidents.summary: Unpublished police data show at least 90 people died working inside Cerro Rico between January and early October 2025, as collapses become more frequent.
incidents.cause: Cave-ins and accidents in cooperative mining; mountain instability
incidents.quote: As of Oct. 3, 96 people had died while working in mining in Potosí department in 2025, with at least 90 of them having died inside Cerro Rico

incidents.place: Potosí, Oruro and La Paz, Bolivia
incidents.affected_desc: about 7,000 children working in gold and silver mines (UNICEF/INE/ILO 2005 study)
incidents.summary: A 2005 UNICEF, national statistics office and ILO study estimated about 7,000 children working in gold and silver mines in Potosí, Oruro and La Paz.
incidents.cause: Poverty; cooperative mining
incidents.quote: approximately7,000 children working in gold and silver mines in the Bolivian cities of Potosí, Oruro and La Paz

incidents.place: Cassiterite mine (Piran Resources), Mwulire, Eastern Province, Rwanda
incidents.affected_desc: seven of the dead were women
incidents.summary: Part of a hill collapsed on miners after heavy rain at a tin (cassiterite) mine in eastern Rwanda, killing 14 people.
incidents.cause: Hill collapse after rain at open mine site
incidents.quote: Fourteen people have been killed in a tin mine in eastern Rwanda after a hill collapsed on them following heavy rains

incidents.place: Rwanda (all mining sites)
incidents.affected_desc: 81 deaths in mining accidents in Rwanda in 2018 (all minerals, quarrying excluded per context)
incidents.summary: Rwanda's mining inspection director said 81 people died in mining accidents in 2018.
incidents.cause: Unsupported underground tunnels; slow implementation of safety standards
incidents.quote: Kanyangira said 81 people died in 2018 in various mining accidents.
incidents.notCounted: Covers all mining in Rwanda, not only tin and coltan, so not added.

incidents.place: Materion (Brush Wellman) primary beryllium plant, Elmore, Ohio, USA
incidents.affected_desc: 6 of 264 short-term workers diagnosed with chronic beryllium disease and 26 sensitized (cohort hired 1993-1999)
incidents.summary: Of 264 short-term workers at the Elmore beryllium plant, 26 were sensitized to beryllium and six had chronic beryllium disease, an incurable lung disease.
incidents.cause: Occupational beryllium exposure
incidents.quote: Sensitization prevalence was 9.8% (26/264), with 6 sensitized also diagnosed with CBD (2.3%, 6/264).

incidents.place: Brush Wellman Elmore plant, Ohio, USA
incidents.affected_desc: spouse of a plant worker developed CBD (take-home exposure)
incidents.summary: The wife of an Elmore plant worker developed chronic beryllium disease, possibly from washing contaminated work clothes.
incidents.cause: Take-home beryllium contamination
incidents.quote: In 1980, the spouse of a Brush Wellman worker at the Elmore Plant developed chronic beryllium disease

incidents.place: Brush Wellman facilities, Ohio, USA
incidents.affected_desc: multiple workers who contracted CBD sued and settled (number not stated in decision)
incidents.summary: Workers who contracted chronic beryllium disease at Brush Wellman sued the company and settled in June 1998.
incidents.cause: Occupational beryllium exposure
incidents.quote: They, among others, sued appellee as a result of contracting Chronic Beryllium Disease

incidents.place: Materion beryllium mill, Delta, Utah, USA
incidents.affected_desc: one mill worker (employed from Aug 2020) diagnosed with beryllium sensitivity; federal compensation claim
incidents.summary: A worker at Materion's Delta, Utah beryllium mill was diagnosed with beryllium sensitivity two years after starting work, according to a federal compensation decision.
incidents.cause: Occupational beryllium exposure
incidents.quote: You were diagnosed with beryllium sensitivity on December 9, 2022.

incidents.place: Y-12 Plant and East Fork Poplar Creek, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, USA
incidents.affected_desc: an estimated 330 metric tons of mercury released to the environment, 110 t of it to East Fork Poplar Creek, from lithium isotope separation
incidents.summary: Lithium enrichment at Y-12 released an estimated 330 tonnes of mercury into the environment, including 110 tonnes into the creek through the town. ATSDR warns that frequent long-term eating of creek fish could harm the nervous system and kidneys.
incidents.cause: US DOE / Y-12 COLEX lithium separation
incidents.quote: Oak Ridge officials estimated that 330 metric tons of mercury were released into the environment; of that total, 110 metric tons were lost to the East Fork Poplar Creek

incidents.place: Thermal Power Plant No. 3, Norilsk; Daldykan/Ambarnaya rivers and Pyasina basin, Taimyr, Russia
incidents.affected_desc: Ust-Avam, an Indigenous village of 450 people, among affected communities
incidents.summary: A fuel tank at a Nornickel power plant failed and spilled about 21,000 tonnes of diesel into Arctic rivers that Indigenous Taimyr communities rely on for fishing.
incidents.cause: Tank failure at Norilsk-Taimyr Energy (Nornickel)
incidents.quote: Ust-Avam is an Indigenous village of 450 people that was impacted by a large fuel spill caused by a subsidiary of Nornickel in May 2020

incidents.place: Farmland around 76 vanadium smelters in 7 regions of China
incidents.affected_desc: children's hazard index above 1 (elevated health risk)
incidents.summary: A national study of farmland around 76 vanadium smelters found metal contamination high enough to raise health risks for children.
incidents.cause: Vanadium smelter emissions and waste
incidents.quote: The Children's hazard index was higher than unity, indicating elevated health risk.

incidents.place: Thacker Pass and other lithium projects, Nevada, USA
incidents.affected_desc: projects advanced without Free, Prior and Informed Consent of affected tribes (Amnesty interviewed 20 Indigenous and Tribal members)
incidents.summary: Amnesty found that the US government is approving new Nevada lithium mines without the free, prior and informed consent of affected Indigenous Peoples.
incidents.cause: US federal government; lithium developers
incidents.quote: moving ahead with a series of new lithium mines across Nevada without the Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) of affected Indigenous Peoples

siteTotals.text: At least 45 people were killed in dated incidents: landslides on 4 June 2024 (20+) and 19 June 2024 (15, with 14 more missing), two miners who died after chemical exposure (2024), a worker buried in 2025, and an explosives-depot blast in October 2026 (7). Myanmar Witness puts the toll for the 2024 rainy season alone at around 50.
siteTotals.basis: calculation: inc-001 (20) + inc-002 (15) + inc-009 (7) = 42; EarthRights gives 'at least 35' for the two June 2024 landslides; Myanmar Witness aggregate of around 50 (May-July 2024) is a source estimate and is not added

siteTotals.text: At least 421 people died in three landslides at Rubaya in nine months, using the lowest reported figure for each: 21 (June 2025), 200 (January 2026) and 200 (March 2026). Reported tolls run to 300+, 226 (up to 400+ in some reports) and 200+ with about 70 children. Amnesty separately documented 18 summary killings of miners at Rubaya and Lomera.
siteTotals.basis: calculation: inc-013 (21) + inc-014 (200) + inc-015 (200) = 421; excludes inc-016 (18 killings, includes Lomera gold site)

siteTotals.text: Trend Asia counted 101 deaths and 240 injuries in 114 incidents at Indonesian nickel facilities from 2015 to mid-2024, nearly half of the deaths at IMIP (40 at IMIP alone). A separate supply-chain mapping report counts 107 deaths and 155 injuries in nickel smelters from 2019 to 2025.
siteTotals.basis: source aggregate (Trend Asia via FT/BHRRC; Mongabay for IMIP 40; Public Citizen GTW for 2019-2025). Dated incidents inc-018 to inc-022 are inside these aggregates; do not add

siteTotals.text: At least 39 people were killed in five dated incidents linked to Grasberg: the 2011 police shooting of strikers (2), the 2013 Big Gossan collapse (28), the 2020 office attack (1), the 2025 mud rush (7) and a 2026 shooting (1).
Nine workers were killed and 30 injured in the 4 May 2022 explosion at Man Maw. No other casualty counts were found.
At least 90 people died working inside Cerro Rico between January and 3 October 2025 (96 across Potosí department), according to unpublished police data.

Fourteen people died in a single 2019 tin mine collapse in Rwanda. Rwanda's mining regulator reports at least 429 deaths and 272 injuries in all mine accidents over five years (to 2023), but these figures are not limited to tin.

exposure.intro: Fusion uses very little of any of these metals. Even 1,500 power plants would use well under 1% of most markets, so fusion does not drive more mining. Its exposure is about where its slice comes from. Choose what is being built to see how much of each material it needs, and how much of that could come from places where harm is documented if fusion bought at the world average.
exposure.method: Market share is a proxy, not a trace. If Indonesia mines 67% of the world's nickel, a randomly sourced kilogram of nickel has about a two-in-three chance of having started there. That is a fair first estimate for fusion because fusion buys a tiny slice of each market (calculations above: <1% even in the high case), so it takes whatever the market mix is. Limits: (1) metals are blended at smelters and refineries, so a given tape's nickel or copper has no single origin; the OECD/IEA traceability report says traders blend 'minerals from diverse origins' and 'blending of materials and reliance on upstream documentation can obscure the true origin' (S67, p.48), and copper 'is often blended during both the smelting and refining stages' (S67). (2) Buyer-specific supply can be far from average: Faraday's tape (Russia/Japan heritage) and Fujikura's GdBCO tape have different rare earths; a Hastelloy mill may buy Class 1 nickel from Canada or Norway, not Indonesian NPI. (3) Mine share is not processing share: China separates most rare earths incl. Myanmar ore, smelts about half of tin and refines 48% of copper, so a 'non-Myanmar' label from a Chinese separator still carries Myanmar risk. (4) Shares for smuggled supply (DRC ore exported as Rwandan; Myanmar estimates from Chinese import data) are themselves estimates. So show it as 'a range of how much could come from these places', not 'how much does'.

devices.note: SPARC holds about 10,000 km of REBCO tape. Our calculation from published tape layer thicknesses, assuming 4 mm-wide tape (inferred from SPARC's 1.5 GA-m over 10,000 km). Magnet copper and steel outside the tape are not included.

yttrium.calc: 10,000 km × 8.2 g/km (5.1–11.9) if all tape were yttrium-based; close to 0 if gadolinium/europium-based tape (e.g. Fujikura) is used.

nickel.calc: 10,000 km × 1.01 kg/km (0.81–2.03): 40–100 µm Hastelloy C-276 substrate, 57% nickel.

silver.calc: 10,000 km × 84–168 g/km: 2–3 µm silver cap layers.

copper-hts.calc: 10,000 km × 0.02–1.43 kg/km: 20 µm copper plating on one or both faces, or none (tape only).

devices.label: ARC-class power plant (10,000–20,000 km of tape)
devices.note: CFS ordered more than 10,000 km of tape from Fujikura for ARC; reporting puts ARC at about twice SPARC's amp-metres, i.e. up to 20,000 km. Our calculation from published tape layer thicknesses, assuming 4 mm-wide tape (inferred from SPARC's 1.5 GA-m over 10,000 km). Fujikura's tape is gadolinium/europium-based, so ARC's yttrium may be close to zero.

yttrium.calc: 15,000 km (10,000–20,000) × 8.2 g/km (5.1–11.9) for yttrium-based tape; near 0 for the Fujikura order.

devices.label: ITER (wire magnets, divertor and first wall)
devices.note: ITER used about 500 t of Nb₃Sn strand (half copper by cross-section). The niobium and tin splits inside the non-copper half are assumptions, not published figures. Divertor tungsten counts only the outer vertical targets. Beryllium is the original first-wall design.

niobium.calc: ASSUMPTION: niobium is 25–50% by weight of the non-copper half of 500 t of strand → 60–125 t.

tin.calc: ASSUMPTION: tin is 10–22% by weight of the non-copper half → 25–55 t over 2008–2015.

tungsten.calc: About 200,000 outer-target monoblocks of about 30×30×10 mm at 19.25 g/cm³, less the cooling-tube bore.

beryllium.calc: About 600 m² of first-wall panels clad in 8–10 mm beryllium tiles (upper bound).

scenarios.label: Announced flagship machines only: 3 ARC-class plants by 2040
scenarios.note: Counted, not modelled: CFS's ARC (early 2030s), the UK's STEP (around 2040), China's next machine after BEST.

scenarios.label: Every company hits its stated date: about 35 pilot plants by 2035
scenarios.note: 35 of 45 companies told the IAEA's 2025 survey they expect a pilot plant in 2030–2035. Treating all as ARC-class overstates it, since not all use HTS magnets.

scenarios.label: Aspirational: 1,500 one-gigawatt plants by 2050 (20% of world power)
scenarios.note: Upper bound from a commentary estimate; larger plants may need more tape than ARC.
